Question 1

Consider the set A, defined as

A={2nn+1:n∈{1,2,3,4}}.

Which of the following sets is equivalent to A?

a
 {1,43,32,85}
b
 {1,43,23,52}
c
 {1,43,54,25}
d
 {1,43,2,32,3}
e
 {1,43,54,65}

decision.explanation: Substituting n=1,2,3,4 into 2n/(n+1) gives 1, 4/3, 3/2, and 8/5, respectively. Thus option a equals A.

history.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2n}{n+1},\,n\in {1,2,3,4}.
$$

Let's write down all the terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =\frac{2(1)}{1+1}=1 \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{2(2)}{2+1}=\frac{4}{3} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{2(3)}{3+1}=\frac{3}{2} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{2(4)}{4+1}=\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A={1,\frac{4}{3},\frac{3}{2},\frac{8}{5}}.
$$

∫−6−1(3f(x)+8)dx=

decision.explanation: Reversing the limits gives ∫ from -6 to -1 of f(x) dx = -9. By linearity, the requested integral is 3(-9)+8(-1-(-6))=-27+40=13.

history.worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{-1}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{-1}^{-6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{-1}(3f(x)+8)\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{-6}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,8{\int }_{-6}^{-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(-9)\,+\,8\cdot x\,{|}_{-6}^{-1} \\  & =-27\,+\,8((-1)-(-6)) \\  & =-27\,+\,40 \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate -5-4i. The numerator becomes 36-45i and the denominator is 25+16=41, giving option d.

history.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-5+4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-5-4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-5-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}} & =\frac{9\text{i}}{-5+4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-5-4\text{i}}{-5-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-45\text{i}-36{\text{i}}^{2}}{{5}^{2}-{4}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-45\text{i}-36(-1)}{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{36-45\text{i}}{25+16} \\  & =\frac{36-45\text{i}}{41}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{36-45\text{i}}{41}=\frac{36}{41}-\frac{45}{41}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14101012/assets/b98d1dd70f315b3059f639c749e83e4679ee9f1fe23682285b789a6e03ee0978.png)

Find the area between the curve $y=-5{x}^{2}+2x-1$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=1$, shown above.
content.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-5{x}^{2}+2x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x-1{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5\cdot {\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}+2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{1}-1\cdot x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-5(\frac{1}{3}-0)+2(\frac{1}{2}-0)-1(1-0) \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}+1-1 \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\frac{5}{3}.$
